7.5 Write property test for unsupported.failingExample:
seed: 24301, path: "1:0:0:0:..." (fast-check), reproducible via { seed: 0x5eed } in the test.

Counterexample (shrunk):
desired = [{ type: 'group', naturalKey: 'a', desired: { name: 'a' } }]
supportedTypes = new Set([])   // membership NOT supported (nor group)
actual = { entities: Map(), memberships: Map([['a', Set(['zzz-extra-member'])]]) }

plan(...) returns an action list that includes a synthesized membership-removal
update: { kind: 'update', resource: { type: 'membership', naturalKey: 'a:zzz-extra-member', desired: { member: false } }, diff: [{ field: 'member', from: true, to: false }] }

This action has type 'membership', which is NOT in supportedTypes, so the
assertion `supportedTypes.has(action.resource.type) === true` for non-skip
actions fails (expected true, received false).

Triage: the test is correct w.r.t. Property 10 / Requirement 7.4 ("report the
unsupported type and skip it"). The counterexample exposes a real gap in
src/seeder/reconciler.ts: planMembershipRemovals() synthesizes membership
'update' actions for undeclared members of a declared group WITHOUT checking
supportedTypes.has('membership'). A group is treated as "declared/authoritative"
when it appears as a `group` resource even if `membership` itself is unsupported,
so removals are emitted for an unsupported type instead of being skipped.

The task hint states these removals "only occur when membership is supported" —
the implementation does not enforce that. Fix (separately, not part of this PBT
task): gate planMembershipRemovals on supportedTypes.has('membership') (and/or
only treat groups as authoritative for removal when membership is supported).
